Tonight I stopped in for dinner on the way home at a local sports eatery. Was tired, but am usually up to stick around for trivia for an hour or two.

An hour or so later, I'm doing so-so (fifth of twelve teams). I at least have a chance of winning if the teams above me gets the last question wrong. And the category is ... The NFL. Fuck.

A murmur in unison echoes throughout the place as eleven of the twelve teams feel confident about THAT category. Meanwhile, twelve pays his tab, puts on his coat to leave, and takes a look at the question:

The NFL played their first game in London in what year? A) 1983 B) 1991 C) 2007 D) 2012

I think I actually know this, so I jot down my answer, hand it in, and go to use the restroom before I leave. A few minutes later I walk out, pass the trivia host as they are cleaning up, and ask, out of curiosity, what the answer was.

"1983"

"Oh cool, so I was right."

"Yeah, you won. Here's your gift certificate."

"Nice. So what place did I come in."

"First. Everyone else got it wrong."

It's the little things. (And luck. Luck helps too.)
I always enjoy when I win trivia games when it's just me against teams of two, three, four, and more.
